name: Ichorene Plant
tags: structure, mining, unraidable, no_saturation_bombardment, bp_cetevska, cetevska, codex_unlockable
desc:
Recovered observations indicate that this facility converts volatile gases into a dense crimson-gray fluid designated Ichorene by intercepted Cetevska communications. The exact production process remains poorly understood.
The refinery itself bears little resemblance to conventional chemical plants. Volatile gases are drawn into vast processing chambers where they disappear into a network of pressurized conduits carrying what appears to be a warm, circulating biological medium. Thermal imaging suggests that much of the facility remains active even during periods of zero production, implying that portions of the installation may themselves be metabolically active.

Every recovered Cetevska casualty has contained significant quantities of Ichorene within its circulatory system, often replacing or supplementing natural blood. Laboratory analysis has confirmed the fluid possesses unusual regenerative and adaptive properties, though its precise composition continues to defy classification. Researchers have proposed that Ichorene acts not merely as a synthetic blood substitute, but as a programmable transport medium capable of assembling increasingly complex organic and mineral structures.

name: Soylent Paste Facility
tags: structure, mining, unraidable, no_saturation_bombardment, bp_cetora, cetora, codex_unlockable
desc:
This installation appears dedicated to the complete recycling of biological matter into standardized nutritional and industrial feedstock. Intercepted Cetoran logistics records refer to the product only as Soylent Paste.
Incoming shipments consist primarily of organic waste, agricultural byproducts, and biological remains unsuitable for conventional processing. Internal scanners suggest that little distinction is made between these categories once they enter the refinement systems. The resulting material is separated into nutritional compounds, industrial organics, and emergency supply reserves with remarkably little measurable waste.
